summary.headline: Codex Vaticanus 1066 Contents
summary.text: Description of Codex Vaticanus 1066, a fifteenth-century paper manuscript containing hippiatric and avian medical texts, including works attributed to Simon, Xenophon, and Apsyrtus, plus an old parchment fragment of St. Basil on Psalms 33 and 44. The catalogue then lists astrological chapters on horoscopes, genethlialogy, the seven stars, zodiacal signs and their rulerships, star forms and animal associations, and the foreknowledge of winds and origins of astronomy.
